intro.en: Cent comes straight from Latin, where it meant a hundred.
intro.cn: cent 直接来自拉丁语，本义是「一百」。

items.en: The Latin word centum means a hundred.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centum 意为「一百」。

items.en: French borrowed the idea in words like centime, a small coin.
items.cn: 法语把这个概念用在 centime（一种小硬币）等词里。

items.en: English adopted cent in the fifteenth century mainly in learned words like per cent.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 cent，主要用于 per cent 等书面词。

items.en: In 1786 the new United States chose cent as the name of its hundredth coin.
items.cn: 一七八六年，新生的美国选定 cent 作为百分之一硬币的名字。

items.en: Today cent also appears in percent, century and centimetre.
items.cn: 如今 cent 还出现在 percent、century 和 centimetre 里。

note.en: These words all carry the cent root meaning hundred, or sound like cent.
note.cn: 这些词都带有表示「百」的 cent 词根，或与 cent 发音相近。

items.en: Later it widened from place to importance: a central idea, a central role.

definition_zh: 确定的；肯定的；必然的；某个；某些
definition_en: sure to happen or be true; fixed and not doubted; a particular thing not named
core_image: 把一块石头放在地上，它绝不会再移动
scene: 考试前我复习了三遍，答案早已记牢。I felt certain about every answer on the test.
sceneCN: 这里 certain 是「确定的」（第 1 个义项：毫不怀疑）；句意是考试前我复习三遍，对每个答案都很有把握。

derivatives.zh: 由 certain 加 -ly 构成，义为「当然；确定地」
由 certain 加 -ty 构成，义为「确定；必然的事」

senses.title: Sure; without doubt
senses.definition: completely sure that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 完全确信某事属实或将会发生
senses.example: I am certain that I locked the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我确信自己锁了门。
senses.why: Something fixed in place cannot move, just as a fact you cannot doubt.
senses.whyCN: 固定不动的石头就像无法怀疑的事实。

senses.title: Sure to happen
senses.definition: certain to happen and impossible to stop or change
senses.definitionCN: 一定会发生、无法阻止或改变的
senses.example: Rain is certain this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 今天下午肯定会下雨。
senses.why: If there is no doubt at all, the result must follow.
senses.whyCN: 若毫无悬念，结果必然到来。

senses.title: A particular one not named

senses.example: A certain student keeps forgetting homework.
senses.exampleCN: 有个学生总是忘带作业。
senses.why: When you know something but keep it vague, the word points without naming.
senses.whyCN: 当你心里有数却不愿点明时，这个词指而不名。

intro.en: Certain means held fast, so doubt cannot shake it.

normal.cn: chain 是环环相连的一串。

normal.en: a chain of events means one thing after another.
normal.cn: a chain of events 表示事情一件接一件。

normal.en: food chain shows who eats whom.
normal.cn: food chain 显示谁吃谁。

normal.en: chain stores share one owner.
normal.cn: chain stores 同属一家公司。

normal.en: chained up means locked with a chain.
normal.cn: chained up 表示用链条锁住。

abstract.en: Picture paper rings glued into a birthday decoration chain.
abstract.cn: 想象彩纸环粘成一串生日装饰。

abstract.en: Picture dominoes falling one after another in a row.
abstract.cn: 想象一排多米诺骨牌依次倒下。

abstract.en: Picture shops with the same sign along a long street.
abstract.cn: 想象长街上一排挂着同一招牌的店铺。

examples.en: I lost the key to the chain that locks my bicycle.
examples.cn: 我弄丢了自行车锁链的钥匙。

examples.en: Wet days started a chain of cancelled football matches.
examples.cn: 连雨天引发了一连串足球赛取消。

examples.en: The gate was chained shut all night.
examples.cn: 大门整夜被链条锁着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「车恩」——骑车人用链条把车锁在栏杆上，车被「恩」住了走不了，所以「车恩」= chain。

root: 拉丁语 catena（链）→ 古法语 chaeine → 英语 chain。与 catenate（连成链）同根。

sensesIntro.en: From metal rings to events, shops and locks.
sensesIntro.cn: 从金属环到事件、商店与锁链。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rings linked one through another
core.cn: 核心意象：环环相扣

intro.en: Chain is a single root, but it builds many phrases.
intro.cn: chain 是单一词根，却能组成许多短语。

latinIntro.en: Latin catena lies behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 catena 是它的源头。

items.example: The joke set off a chain reaction of laughter.
items.exampleCN: 笑话引发了连锁的笑声。

items.meaning: one shop of a big group
items.example: The bookstore chain has forty shops.
items.exampleCN: 这家连锁书店有四十家门店。

items.example: My key chain has a small bell.
items.exampleCN: 我的钥匙链上有个小铃铛。
锁着的自行车安然无恙。

items.meaning: one who lights the next cigarette at once
items.exampleCN: 李叔叔抽烟一根接一根。
解了链的狗欢快地跑着。

definition_zh: 便宜地；廉价地；花费少地
definition_en: in a way that costs little money; at a low price
core_image: 用几张零钱就把东西拎回家
scene: 文具店打折，我三块钱买到了两支钢笔。I managed to buy two pens quite cheaply at the sale.
sceneCN: 这里 cheaply 是「便宜地」（第 1 个义项：花钱少）；句意是我在促销时便宜地买了两支钢笔。

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词基础，义为「便宜的」
由 cheap 加 -ness 构成，义为「便宜；廉价」
cheap 的比较级，义为「更便宜的」

senses.title: At a low price
senses.definition: in a way that costs only a little money
senses.definitionCN: 花钱很少的方式
senses.example: Students can eat cheaply at the school canteen.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在学校食堂吃饭很省钱。
senses.why: The word takes cheap and turns the low price into a manner.
senses.whyCN: 它把 cheap 的低价变成一种方式。

senses.title: With little effort or cost of quality
senses.definition: made with poor materials in order to save money
senses.definitionCN: 为省钱而用料低劣地制作
senses.example: The toy was cheaply made and broke in a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这玩具做工廉价，一天就坏了。
senses.why: Low price sometimes walks hand in hand with low quality.
senses.whyCN: 低价有时与低质相伴。

senses.title: Without wasting money
senses.definition: carefully, so money is not wasted
senses.definitionCN: 精打细算、不浪费钱地
senses.example: Our family travels cheaply by taking night trains.
senses.exampleCN: 我们家坐夜车旅行，节省开支。
senses.why: Spending little can also mean spending wisely.
senses.whyCN: 花得少也可以是花得聪明。

intro.en: Cheap comes from an old word for trade, not for price.
intro.cn: cheap 源自表示「交易」的古词，而非「价格」。

items.en: Old English ceap meant trade, buying and selling.
items.cn: 古英语 ceap 意为交易、买卖。

items.en: Chipping, now a London street name, once meant a market.
items.cn: Chipping（伦敦街名）曾意为市场。

items.en: At the market, goods that sold at good bargains came to be called cheap.
items.cn: 市场上讨价好成交的货物渐渐被称为 cheap。

items.en: The sense narrowed from the trade itself to the low price.
items.cn: 词义从「交易」收窄为「低价」。

items.en: The adverb cheaply formed with the common -ly ending.
items.cn: 副词 cheaply 按常见规则加 -ly 构成。

note.en: One family about low prices and smart spending.
note.cn: 围绕低价与精打细算的词族。

entries.definition: to act dishonestly; similar letters, different word
the tiny sound of a baby bird; sounds the same

normalIntro.en: Start from cheap, then add the adverb tail.
normalIntro.cn: 从 cheap 出发，再加副词尾巴。

normal.en: cheap means costing little.
normal.cn: cheap 意为便宜。

normal.en: cheaply = cheap + -ly, in a cheap way.
normal.cn: cheaply 由 cheap 加 -ly 构成，便宜地。

normal.en: buy cheaply, spend less.
normal.cn: buy cheaply 就是花得少。

normal.en: cheaply made can mean badly made.
normal.cn: cheaply made 有时指做工差。

normal.en: cheaper is the comparing form of cheap.
normal.cn: cheaper 是 cheap 的比较级。

abstract.en: Picture two heavy bags: one costs ten coins, one costs two.
abstract.cn: 想象两个大袋子：一个花十枚硬币，一个只花两枚。

abstract.en: Picture a coin pig that smiles when you save at the market.
abstract.cn: 想象市场省钱时存钱罐露出笑容。

abstract.en: Picture a cheap toy snapping apart the first time you play.
abstract.cn: 想象廉价玩具一玩就散架。

examples.en: We can eat cheaply at the noodle shop near school.
examples.cn: 在学校附近的面馆吃饭很便宜。

examples.en: Second-hand books let us study cheaply.
examples.cn: 二手书让我们低成本地学习。

examples.en: The bag looked good but was cheaply sewn.
examples.cn: 这包看着不错，但缝制得很廉价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欺普利」——用很少的钱欺负了普通价格，捡了大便宜，所以「欺普利」= cheaply。

root: 古英语 ceap（交易）→ 中古英语 cheap（低价买到）→ cheap + -ly。与 chapman（小贩）、Chipping 街名同源。

sensesIntro.en: Low price, low quality, or wise saving.
sensesIntro.cn: 低价、廉价或节俭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money staying in your pocket
core.cn: 核心意象：钱留在口袋里

intro.en: Cheap builds a small but useful family.
intro.cn: cheap 构成的词族不大但实用。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, so no Latin cousins exist here.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语源，此处没有拉丁同族词。

items.example: Cheaply means in a cheap way.
This pen is cheaper than that one.
The cheapest seat is still good.

items.exampleCN: 他们廉价修好了自行车。

definition_zh: 欺骗；作弊；骗取；骗子
definition_en: to act dishonestly to win or gain something; a dishonest person
core_image: 把袖子里藏的另一张牌悄悄换出来
scene: 同桌考试时偷偷瞟我的卷子，被老师发现了。He tried to cheat in the exam by looking at my paper.
sceneCN: 这里 cheat 是「作弊」（第 1 个义项：不诚实地取利）；句意是他想偷看我的卷子作弊，被老师发现。

derivatives.zh: 由 cheat 加 -er 构成，义为「骗子；作弊者」
由 cheat 加 -ing 构成，义为「作弊；欺骗行为」
由 cheat 加 sheet 构成，义为「小抄」

senses.title: To break rules secretly to win
senses.definition: to act against rules in a game, exam or sport without being seen
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、考试或运动中暗中违反规则
senses.example: He cheated by hiding notes in his sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 他把小抄藏在袖子里作弊。
senses.why: Winning unfairly needs hiding, like a card swapped from a sleeve.
senses.whyCN: 不公平地赢需要遮掩，就像从袖子里换牌。

senses.title: To trick someone for gain
senses.definition: to make someone believe something false so you gain
senses.definitionCN: 使某人信假话以从中获利
senses.example: A stranger cheated my grandmother out of two hundred yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 一个陌生人骗了我奶奶两百元。
senses.why: The trick pulls money or trust out of another's pocket.
senses.whyCN: 花招从别人的口袋里掏走钱或信任。

senses.title: A dishonest person or act
senses.definition: a person who cheats, or the act itself
senses.definitionCN: 行骗的人或行为本身
senses.example: Nobody wants to play cards with a cheat.
senses.exampleCN: 没人愿意和骗子打牌。
senses.why: The doer and the deed share one short word.
senses.whyCN: 做坏事的人和坏事共用这个短词。

intro.en: Cheat grew out of the word escheat, a lawyer's term.
intro.cn: cheat 由法律术语 escheat 蜕变而来。

items.en: Old French escheat meant property that falls to the lord when its owner dies without heirs.
items.cn: 古法语 escheat 指无人继承时归于领主的财产。

items.en: English borrowed escheat for the same legal meaning.
items.cn: 英语借入 escheat 表示同样的法律意义。

items.en: Lawyers shortened the noun to cheat.
items.cn: 法律界人士把该名词缩略为 cheat。

items.en: Cheat then meant the fraudulent getting of another's property.
items.cn: cheat 随后指用欺诈手段夺取他人财产。

items.en: The verb widened to cheating in games, love and study.
items.cn: 动词用法扩展到游戏、感情和学习中的欺骗。

note.en: Close spellings and close meanings of dishonesty.
note.cn: 与「不诚实」形近义近的词。

entries.definition: a baby bird's sound; same sound
a sheet of information; letters close, no relation
to make someone believe what is false
to fool someone, often less seriously
serious dishonest gain, often legal word

normalIntro.en: One short word hiding a dishonest act.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词里藏着不光彩的行为。

normal.en: cheat means to win by breaking rules.
normal.cn: cheat 指靠违规取胜。

normal.en: cheat in an exam is copying or hiding notes.
normal.cn: 考试作弊就是抄袭或藏小抄。

normal.en: cheat somebody out of money takes money by tricks.
normal.cn: cheat somebody out of money 用花招骗钱。

normal.en: a cheat is the dishonest person.
normal.cn: a cheat 指骗子。

normal.en: cheat sounds like cheap with a t.
normal.cn: cheat 听起来像 cheap 换了个 t。

abstract.en: Picture extra cards slipping out of a card player's sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想象牌桌旁从袖口滑出的多余牌。

abstract.en: Picture a student's eyes sliding sideways toward another's paper.
abstract.cn: 想象学生的视线偷偷滑向别人的卷子。

abstract.en: Picture a false coin glittering in a market hand.
abstract.cn: 想象市场里一只手闪烁着假硬币。

examples.en: She refused to cheat even when the test was hard.
examples.cn: 即使考试很难，她也拒绝作弊。

examples.en: The old man was cheated by a fake phone call.
examples.cn: 老人被一通假电话骗了。

examples.en: Cheats never win real respect.
examples.cn: 骗子永远赢不来真正的尊重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欺特」——他专门欺负特别信任他的人，用花招骗人，所以「欺特」= cheat。

root: 古法语 escheat（无主财产归领主）→ 中古英语 escheat 缩略为 cheat（欺诈取得）→ 动词、名词。与 escheat 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Secret rule-breaking, tricking for gain, and the dishonest person.
sensesIntro.cn: 暗中违规、骗取利益与行骗之人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: winning with a hidden false card
core.cn: 核心意象：用暗藏的假牌取胜

branches.en: Breaking rules in tests and games

intro.en: Cheat works alone and inside honest-family opposites.
intro.cn: cheat 可独立使用，也可与反义词族对照。

latinIntro.en: The source is Old French law, not Latin stems.
latinIntro.cn: 源头是古法语法律用语，而非拉丁词干。

items.example: The cheater lost all his friends.
items.exampleCN: 那个骗子失去了所有朋友。

items.example: Cheating is punished in our school.
items.exampleCN: 我们学校对作弊有处罚。

items.example: The teacher found his cheat sheet.
A dishonest player spoils the game.
items.exampleCN: 不诚实的玩家毁掉比赛。

items.example: He tricked me with a false story.

latinEntries.meaning: to fall away, source of escheat
latinEntries.meaningCN: 落出、脱落（escheat 的拉丁源头）

definition_zh: 碎片；薯条；芯片；削下碎片；碰缺
definition_en: a small broken piece; a thin fried potato; a tiny electronic circuit; to break a small piece off
core_image: 从大块上崩下来的一小片
scene: 厨房里，妈妈正把土豆切成细条准备炸。My mother dropped a chip of potato into the hot oil.
sceneCN: 这里 chip 是「薯条」（第 2 个义项：油炸土豆条）；句意是妈妈把一根土豆条放进热油里。

derivatives.zh: 由 micro- 加 chip 构成，义为「微型芯片」
由 chip 加 -ed 构成，义为「有缺口的；破碎的」
由 chip 加 -y 构成，义为「炸鱼薯条店（英式口语）」

senses.title: A small broken piece
senses.definition: a small piece broken off something hard
senses.definitionCN: 从坚硬物上崩下来的小块
senses.example: A chip of paint fell on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一块油漆碎片掉在地板上。
senses.why: A knock breaks a little piece away from the whole.
senses.whyCN: 一磕碰，就从整体上崩下小片。

senses.title: A thin piece of fried potato
senses.definition: a long thin piece of potato cooked in oil
senses.definitionCN: 油炸的细长土豆条
senses.example: We shared a bag of chips after school.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后我们分吃了一包薯条。
senses.why: The potato is cut into small slips, like chips of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 土豆被切成小条，就像整块上的碎条。

senses.title: A tiny electronic circuit
senses.definition: a very small flat piece inside computers that holds circuits
senses.definitionCN: 计算机内部承载电路的微型薄片
senses.example: This phone uses a faster chip.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机用了更快的芯片。
senses.why: The little silicon slip is a chip of the whole machine's brain.
senses.whyCN: 这片小小的硅片是机器大脑的一小块。

senses.title: To break a small piece off
senses.definition: to lose or remove a small piece from an edge or surface
senses.definitionCN: 使边缘或表面脱落一小块
senses.example: Don't chip the paint on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 别把课桌上的漆碰掉了。
senses.why: One careless hit takes a bite out of the edge.
senses.whyCN: 一次不小心磕碰就啃掉一块边。

intro.en: Chip has always meant a small piece cut or broken off.
intro.cn: chip 一直表示切下或崩下的小片。

items.en: Old English cipp meant a thin piece of wood, a beam or chip.
items.cn: 古英语 cipp 指薄木片、木条。

items.en: The word kept its wooden sense through the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 整个中世纪该词保留木片之义。

items.en: Wooden chips led to fried potato chips, named for their shape.
items.cn: 木片引申出炸薯条，因其形状得名。

items.en: British English keeps chips for fries; American chips are crisps.
items.cn: 英式 chips 指薯条；美式 chips 指薯片。

items.en: In the twentieth century the tiny silicon circuit borrowed the same small-piece idea.
items.cn: 二十世纪，微型硅电路借用了同一「小片」概念。

note.en: Small pieces and near spellings.
note.cn: 小碎片与形近词。

entries.definition: a large boat; one letter apart
a broken part of something larger
a tiny piece of bread or cake
a small light piece that falls off

normalIntro.en: Every sense is a small piece of something bigger.
normalIntro.cn: 每个义项都是更大之物的一小片。

normal.en: chip = a small piece broken off.
normal.cn: chip 是崩下来的小片。

normal.en: fish and chips is a famous British meal.
normal.cn: fish and chips 是著名英式餐。

normal.en: a computer chip holds tiny circuits.
normal.cn: computer chip 承载微小电路。

normal.en: chip off means to break a piece away.
normal.cn: chip off 表示崩掉一块。

normal.en: a chipped cup has a broken edge.
normal.cn: chipped cup 的边缘缺了一块。

abstract.en: Picture paint flakes fluttering off an old door.
abstract.cn: 想象旧门上剥落飘下的漆片。

abstract.en: Picture hot golden fries steaming in a paper bag.
abstract.cn: 想象纸袋里冒着热气的金黄薯条。

abstract.en: Picture a coin-sized black square on a green circuit board.
abstract.cn: 想象绿色电路板上硬币大小的黑色方块。

examples.en: A chip of the bowl went into the sink.
examples.cn: 碗的一块碎片掉进了水槽。

examples.en: The edge of my chair is chipped from years of use.
examples.cn: 椅子边缘因常年使用缺了一块。

examples.en: Our new tablet has a chip that saves battery.
examples.cn: 我们的新平板有一块省电的芯片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「砌普」——砌墙时崩下来的小碎片叫 chip，碎片像薯条又像芯片，都是「砌普」下来的。

root: 古英语 cipp（薄木片）→ 中古英语 chip → 现代英语扩展出薯条、芯片等义。日耳曼语源，无拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: One little piece becomes food, technology and damage.
sensesIntro.cn: 一小片演化为食物、科技与破损。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small piece broken from a whole
core.cn: 核心意象：从整体崩落的一小片

branches.en: Bits of wood, paint and glass

intro.en: Chip pairs with micro- in modern technology.
intro.cn: chip 在现代科技中与 micro- 组合。

latinIntro.en: The root is Old English, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词根出自古英语，拉丁同族为空。

items.example: Chips of wood covered the ground.

items.exampleCN: 每部手机都有许多微芯片。

items.meaning: with a small piece broken off
items.example: The chipped plate is still useful.

items.meaning: the act of breaking bits off
to join in or give help
items.example: We all chipped in for the gift.
Chop the carrots for the soup.

items.exampleCN: 比起薯条我更喜欢薯片。

definition_zh: 经典的；典型的；古典的；经典作品
definition_en: very typical of its kind; of the highest quality over a long time; a famous work
core_image: 被一代代人翻旧了却永远摆在书架正中的那本书
scene: 音乐教室里响起一首大家都会哼的老歌。That song is a classic that every student knows.
sceneCN: 这里 classic 是「经典作品」（第 3 个义项：经久不衰的名作）；句意是那首歌是学生都会的经典。

derivatives.zh: 由 classic 加 -al 构成，义为「古典的；传统的」
由 classical 加 -ly 构成，义为「经典地；传统地」
classic 复数形式，义为「经典作品；古典学科」

senses.title: Very typical
senses.definition: showing the most usual qualities of a kind
senses.definitionCN: 表现出某类事物最典型特征
senses.example: That is a classic case of forgetting homework.
senses.exampleCN: 那是忘带作业的典型例子。
senses.why: The example fits its class so well it stands for all.
senses.whyCN: 这个例子与同类如此吻合，足可代表全部。

senses.title: Of lasting high quality
senses.definition: excellent in a way that lasts for many years
senses.definitionCN: 多年不衰的优秀品质
senses.example: Her classic red dress never goes out of fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 她的经典红裙永不过时。
senses.why: Quality that survives time earns the word classic.
senses.whyCN: 经得起时间检验的品质才配得上经典。

senses.title: A famous work or thing
senses.definition: a book, film or song that stays famous for years
senses.definitionCN: 长年闻名不衰的书、电影或歌曲
senses.example: Treasure Island is a children's classic.
senses.exampleCN: 《金银岛》是儿童文学经典。
senses.why: Works loved across generations become classics.
senses.whyCN: 跨越几代人仍被喜爱的作品便成经典。

intro.en: Classic comes from the Roman word for the highest class of citizens.
intro.cn: classic 源自罗马语中「最高等级公民」的说法。

items.en: Latin classicus meant of the highest rank or class.
items.cn: 拉丁语 classicus 意为最高等级的。

items.en: It comes from classis, a division of the Roman people.
items.cn: 它来自 classis，即罗马公民的等级划分。

items.en: French formed classique, praising first-rank writers.
